I'm gonna go out on a limb here and recommend traditional roguelikes. They are turn based so you can take as long as you want. Blind and even severely disabled gamers are able to play them. There is a ton of emergent gameplay too.

EDIT: Also, don't forget using peripherals like steering wheels and pedals. Playing ETS2 or ATS is amazing while listening to music. Without music, it's OK, but with music it improves the experience exponentially.
Do you have any traditional roguelike that you recommend?

Rogue (obviously - I'm sure you can find it somewhere), Castle of the Winds, Unreal World, Slash'EM, CataclysmDDA (I've really enjoyed this one).

If you're new to roguelikes, I'd recommend Dungeons of Dredmor. It's less traditional, definitely better graphics (read, non-ascii graphics), and has a sense of humor. I think you can play it with one hand, though.

If you're good at rhythm games, you might give Crypt of the Necrodancer a try, too. It's a roguelike/rhythm game mash.

And if you're feeling particularly self-loathing, Dwarf Fortress' adventure mode is sort of a roguelike, and I can see it being played with one hand.
